modules.name: Path chapters
modules.description: Guided capabilities for building, grounding, testing, deploying, and extending your AI app.

tracks.name: Define
tracks.description: Shape the outcome, users, corpus, safety boundaries, and demo story.

tracks.name: Foundations
tracks.description: Provision Foundry, choose a model, create an agent, and ground it with knowledge.

tracks.name: Action Tools
tracks.description: Attach governed tools and approval-gated workflows.

tracks.name: Trust
tracks.description: Evaluate, red-team, trace, and debug agent behavior.

tracks.name: Deploy
tracks.description: Host the agent and expose a stakeholder-ready experience.

tracks.name: Orchestrate
tracks.description: Coordinate multiple agents with manager, planner, and router patterns.

tracks.name: Extras
tracks.description: Optional deepeners for UI, voice, Fabric IQ, long-running agents, and Copilot-assisted work.

outcomes.name: Need an idea first
outcomes.tagline: Generate a ranked, buildable AI application idea before starting the customer build path.
outcomes.description: Use Activity Forge to pick a right-sized idea with clear users, safe data, one action, and a believable demo.
success_metrics: A selected idea has an outcome, users, data sources, tier guidance, and risk notes.
The chosen idea transfers cleanly into the Customer Build scenario pack.

outcomes.name: Learn with Northfield
outcomes.tagline: Practice the full Foundry path with the known-good Northfield University reference scenario.
outcomes.description: Build the Northfield IQ Assistant, then reuse the same architecture for customer work later.
success_metrics: The Northfield assistant is grounded, action-capable, evaluated, observable, and deployable.
Participants can identify what to swap when moving from Northfield to a customer scenario.

outcomes.name: Bring your own customer outcome
outcomes.tagline: Turn a real customer-safe scenario into a grounded, evaluated Foundry agent prototype.
outcomes.description: Define the outcome, swap in your own corpus and persona, add one governed action, prove trust, and demo the result.
success_metrics: The team can explain the target users, corpus, action, safety boundaries, and demo story.
The prototype answers with citations, acts only through governed tools, and has a trust scorecard.

paths.name: Knowledge and policy assistant
paths.tagline: Answer from trusted, approved sources with clear citations and abstention.
paths.description: Choose this path when the primary customer value is reliable answers about policies, manuals, FAQs, or other governed knowledge.

sessions.note: Define users, approved sources, access assumptions, and abstention boundaries.
sessions.title: Define your outcome
sessions.description: Create the scenario pack: users, outcome, corpus, safe action, success measures, and demo story.

sessions.label: Build the agent and knowledge base
sessions.note: Complete Steps 1-4, including Foundry IQ grounding.
sessions.title: Ground: Foundations
sessions.description: Provision Foundry, choose a model, create an agent, and ground it with the Northfield FAQ corpus.

sessions.note: Test cited answers, abstention, and domain-specific safety.
sessions.title: Prove: Evaluation & Red Teaming
sessions.description: Build quality and safety evals, run adversarial prompts, and gate the agent with a scorecard.

sessions.note: Show retrieval, latency, and failure paths.
sessions.title: Debug: Tracing & Observability
sessions.description: Trace model calls, retrieval, tool use, and failures in Application Insights.

sessions.note: Expose a controlled endpoint for stakeholder testing.
sessions.title: Deploy: Hosted Agent
sessions.description: Package and deploy your agent as a hosted endpoint with the unified azure.yaml contract.

sessions.note: Use only when a visible citations experience strengthens the demo.
sessions.title: Demo UI: Build a UI
sessions.description: Create a stakeholder-facing chat or demo UI for the Foundry agent.

sessions.note: Add only a clearly governed side effect; knowledge alone is enough for this path.
sessions.title: Act: Action Tools
sessions.description: Attach governed tools and approval-gated actions to your Foundry agent.

paths.name: Governed action and workflow agent
paths.tagline: Turn an approved request into one safe, reviewable workflow action.
paths.description: Choose this path when value comes from creating, changing, routing, or escalating work rather than answering from a document corpus.

sessions.note: Define the side effect, requester, approver, escalation, and evidence.
sessions.title: Define your outcome
sessions.description: Create the scenario pack: users, outcome, corpus, safe action, success measures, and demo story.

sessions.label: Provision and define the agent
sessions.note: Complete Steps 1-3. Knowledge-base Step 4 is optional unless the action needs policy context.
sessions.title: Ground: Foundations
sessions.description: Provision Foundry, choose a model, create an agent, and ground it with the Northfield FAQ corpus.

sessions.note: Implement one small approval-gated action or safe draft/queue equivalent.
sessions.title: Act: Action Tools
sessions.description: Attach governed tools and approval-gated actions to your Foundry agent.

sessions.note: Evaluate call, deny, escalate, and refusal behavior.
sessions.title: Prove: Evaluation & Red Teaming
sessions.description: Build quality and safety evals, run adversarial prompts, and gate the agent with a scorecard.

sessions.note: Trace tool calls and approval decisions end to end.
sessions.title: Debug: Tracing & Observability
sessions.description: Trace model calls, retrieval, tool use, and failures in Application Insights.

sessions.note: Host the controlled workflow for stakeholder testing.
sessions.title: Deploy: Hosted Agent
sessions.description: Package and deploy your agent as a hosted endpoint with the unified azure.yaml contract.

sessions.note: Add when users need an approval card or workflow status surface.
sessions.title: Demo UI: Build a UI
sessions.description: Create a stakeholder-facing chat or demo UI for the Foundry agent.

sessions.note: Use for work that must survive the request or browser session.
sessions.title: Deploy: Long-Running Agents
sessions.description: Use background run patterns for workflows that outlive a browser session.

paths.name: Document workflow
paths.tagline: Extract, validate, review, and route structured work from documents.
paths.description: Choose this path when documents begin a business process and a human must be able to see, correct, and approve the extracted result.

sessions.note: Define approved document types, retention, reviewers, unacceptable extraction errors, and the route after review.
sessions.title: Define your outcome
sessions.description: Create the scenario pack: users, outcome, corpus, safe action, success measures, and demo story.

sessions.label: Provision and define the agent
sessions.note: Complete Steps 1-3. A knowledge base is optional unless the workflow needs policy context.
sessions.title: Ground: Foundations
sessions.description: Provision Foundry, choose a model, create an agent, and ground it with the Northfield FAQ corpus.

sessions.note: Build extraction, confidence validation, review, and structured handoff for one safe document type.
sessions.title: Build: Document Workflow
sessions.description: Extract, validate, review, and route document data with a keyless, human-governed workflow.

sessions.note: Test extraction quality, low-confidence handling, prompt injection in documents, and review routing.
sessions.title: Prove: Evaluation & Red Teaming
sessions.description: Build quality and safety evals, run adversarial prompts, and gate the agent with a scorecard.

sessions.note: Trace document processing, validation, and reviewer decisions.
sessions.title: Debug: Tracing & Observability
sessions.description: Trace model calls, retrieval, tool use, and failures in Application Insights.

sessions.note: Host the controlled workflow only after document and reviewer access are understood.
sessions.title: Deploy: Hosted Agent
sessions.description: Package and deploy your agent as a hosted endpoint with the unified azure.yaml contract.

sessions.note: Add a review surface only when it makes correction and approval clearer.
sessions.title: Demo UI: Build a UI
sessions.description: Create a stakeholder-facing chat or demo UI for the Foundry agent.

paths.name: Live data and insights copilot
paths.tagline: Answer right-now operational questions from a governed live data source.
paths.description: Choose this path when the customer needs current state, capacity, inventory, queue, SLA, or metric insight rather than static policy retrieval.

sessions.note: Define the source of truth, allowed fields, freshness expectation, and access boundary.
sessions.title: Define your outcome
sessions.description: Create the scenario pack: users, outcome, corpus, safe action, success measures, and demo story.

sessions.label: Provision and define the agent
sessions.note: Complete Steps 1-3. Add a static knowledge base only when policy context is also needed.
sessions.title: Ground: Foundations
sessions.description: Provision Foundry, choose a model, create an agent, and ground it with the Northfield FAQ corpus.

sessions.note: Connect the approved operational data path and prove source routing.
sessions.title: Deepen: Fabric IQ
sessions.description: Ground answers in operational or analytical data when static documents are not enough.

sessions.note: Test factuality, access boundaries, and safe handling of missing or stale data.
sessions.title: Prove: Evaluation & Red Teaming
sessions.description: Build quality and safety evals, run adversarial prompts, and gate the agent with a scorecard.

sessions.note: Trace live-data tool selection and latency.
sessions.title: Debug: Tracing & Observability
sessions.description: Trace model calls, retrieval, tool use, and failures in Application Insights.

sessions.note: Host the copilot for a controlled user trial.
sessions.title: Deploy: Hosted Agent
sessions.description: Package and deploy your agent as a hosted endpoint with the unified azure.yaml contract.

sessions.note: Use when a data-oriented stakeholder experience improves the proof point.
sessions.title: Demo UI: Build a UI
sessions.description: Create a stakeholder-facing chat or demo UI for the Foundry agent.

paths.name: Voice assistant
paths.tagline: Deliver a low-friction spoken interaction without weakening the agent contract.
paths.description: Choose this path when voice, accessibility, hands-free use, or a live conversational experience is central to the customer outcome.

sessions.note: Define audience, language, accessibility needs, handoff behavior, and the safe spoken demo.
sessions.title: Define your outcome
sessions.description: Create the scenario pack: users, outcome, corpus, safe action, success measures, and demo story.

sessions.label: Provision and define the agent
sessions.note: Complete Steps 1-3. Grounding is optional unless spoken answers need trusted source citations.
sessions.title: Ground: Foundations
sessions.description: Provision Foundry, choose a model, create an agent, and ground it with the Northfield FAQ corpus.

sessions.note: Bind Voice Live to the scenario agent and tune turn-taking.
sessions.title: Interface: Voice Live
sessions.description: Add a spoken interaction path for contact-center, accessibility, or demo scenarios.

sessions.note: Test safety, refusal, and task completion in the spoken experience.
sessions.title: Prove: Evaluation & Red Teaming
sessions.description: Build quality and safety evals, run adversarial prompts, and gate the agent with a scorecard.

sessions.note: Make latency and failed interaction paths visible.
sessions.title: Debug: Tracing & Observability
sessions.description: Trace model calls, retrieval, tool use, and failures in Application Insights.

sessions.note: Host the agent for a repeatable voice demo.
sessions.title: Deploy: Hosted Agent
sessions.description: Package and deploy your agent as a hosted endpoint with the unified azure.yaml contract.

sessions.note: Add a companion transcript or handoff surface when it helps the user journey.
sessions.title: Demo UI: Build a UI
sessions.description: Create a stakeholder-facing chat or demo UI for the Foundry agent.

paths.description: Choose this path when a user needs help understanding an image and the outcome can be bounded with explicit uncertainty and review behavior.

sessions.note: Define allowed image classes, privacy boundaries, unsupported cases, reviewers, and the safe proof scenario.
sessions.title: Define your outcome
sessions.description: Create the scenario pack: users, outcome, corpus, safe action, success measures, and demo story.

sessions.label: Provision and define the agent
sessions.note: Complete Steps 1-3; add document grounding only if the image result needs policy context.
sessions.title: Ground: Foundations
sessions.description: Provision Foundry, choose a model, create an agent, and ground it with the Northfield FAQ corpus.

sessions.note: Build structured image analysis with uncertainty and human-review boundaries.
sessions.title: Build: Visual Multimodal
sessions.description: Analyze safe image inputs with structured results, uncertainty handling, and human review boundaries.

sessions.note: Test correct interpretation, uncertainty, unsafe inputs, and escalation.
sessions.title: Prove: Evaluation & Red Teaming
sessions.description: Build quality and safety evals, run adversarial prompts, and gate the agent with a scorecard.

sessions.note: Trace image processing and failure paths without exposing unsafe content.
sessions.title: Debug: Tracing & Observability
sessions.description: Trace model calls, retrieval, tool use, and failures in Application Insights.

sessions.note: Host only the approved, access-controlled experience.
sessions.title: Deploy: Hosted Agent
sessions.description: Package and deploy your agent as a hosted endpoint with the unified azure.yaml contract.

sessions.note: Use when the result needs a clear, reviewable visual interface.
sessions.title: Demo UI: Build a UI
sessions.description: Create a stakeholder-facing chat or demo UI for the Foundry agent.

paths.name: Governed data copilot
paths.tagline: Answer structured-data questions through explicit access, field, and provenance controls.
paths.description: Choose this path when operational insight needs more governance than a generic live-data lookup: approved fields, query rules, access assumptions, and explainable results.

sessions.note: Define the data owner, approved fields, requester access, unacceptable disclosures, and a trustworthy result proof.
sessions.title: Define your outcome
sessions.description: Create the scenario pack: users, outcome, corpus, safe action, success measures, and demo story.

sessions.label: Provision and define the agent
sessions.note: Complete Steps 1-3. Static knowledge is optional and may supply policy context.
sessions.title: Ground: Foundations
sessions.description: Provision Foundry, choose a model, create an agent, and ground it with the Northfield FAQ corpus.

sessions.note: Implement allowlisted structured-data access, query validation, provenance, and sensitive-result review.
sessions.title: Build: Governed Data Copilot
sessions.description: Query approved structured data through explicit access, field, and result-provenance controls.

sessions.note: Test access denial, unsafe query attempts, unsupported questions, and result correctness.
sessions.title: Prove: Evaluation & Red Teaming
sessions.description: Build quality and safety evals, run adversarial prompts, and gate the agent with a scorecard.

sessions.note: Trace the governed query path and inspect denied or escalated requests.
sessions.title: Debug: Tracing & Observability
sessions.description: Trace model calls, retrieval, tool use, and failures in Application Insights.

sessions.note: Expose only after caller identity and data-platform permissions are decided.
sessions.title: Deploy: Hosted Agent
sessions.description: Package and deploy your agent as a hosted endpoint with the unified azure.yaml contract.

sessions.note: Use when results need a visible provenance and approval surface.
sessions.title: Demo UI: Build a UI
sessions.description: Create a stakeholder-facing chat or demo UI for the Foundry agent.

sessions.note: Use Fabric IQ when the governed source is a supported Fabric/OneLake workload.
sessions.title: Deepen: Fabric IQ
sessions.description: Ground answers in operational or analytical data when static documents are not enough.

paths.name: Orchestrated or long-running workflow
paths.tagline: Coordinate specialist work when a single agent or one chat turn is not enough.
paths.description: Choose this path when the outcome has real handoffs, specialist roles, durable jobs, or an auditable multi-step process.

sessions.note: Define role boundaries, handoffs, ownership, and the smallest valuable end-to-end process.
sessions.title: Define your outcome
sessions.description: Create the scenario pack: users, outcome, corpus, safe action, success measures, and demo story.

sessions.label: Provision and define the agent
sessions.note: Complete Steps 1-3. Add grounding only to specialists that need trusted documents.
sessions.title: Ground: Foundations

sessions.note: Model the manager/planner workflow before adding concurrency.

sessions.note: Build the smallest router and specialist team that proves the outcome.
sessions.title: Orchestrate: Multi-Agent Capstone

sessions.note: Evaluate routing, handoffs, refusals, and final task completion.
sessions.title: Prove: Evaluation & Red Teaming
sessions.description: Build quality and safety evals, run adversarial prompts, and gate the agent with a scorecard.

sessions.note: Trace handoffs and investigate failed paths.
sessions.title: Debug: Tracing & Observability
sessions.description: Trace model calls, retrieval, tool use, and failures in Application Insights.

sessions.note: Add only if a specialist must safely change a downstream system.
sessions.title: Act: Action Tools
sessions.description: Attach governed tools and approval-gated actions to your Foundry agent.

sessions.note: Use when the workflow must continue after the initiating request ends.
sessions.title: Deploy: Long-Running Agents
sessions.description: Use background run patterns for workflows that outlive a browser session.

sessions.note: Host the workflow behind a controlled endpoint.
sessions.title: Deploy: Hosted Agent
